root_cause_label: Incorrect Domain Interpretation and Field Selection
one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent filtered by the literal domain label 'science' (which does not exist in the dataset) instead of biology/chemistry/physics, and counted only deepseek_reasoning tokens instead of also including deepseek_solution, resulting in a wrong final token count.
t_err_evidence: Step 9 executes the first full token-counting script filtering with domain == 'science' (case-insensitive) and tokenizing only the 'messages' fallback field, without having read the README that shows the 'metadata' config contains 'deepseek_reasoning'/'deepseek_solution' and that there is no 'science' domain label.
t_commit_evidence: Step 28 is the last substantive implementation step; while it corrects the domain filter to biology/chemistry/physics, it still only counts deepseek_reasoning and omits deepseek_solution, locking in an incorrect partial token count regardless of subsequent verification steps.
t_surface_evidence: Step 21: 'cat: /app/answer.txt: No such file or directory' — first observable signal that none of the prior token-counting scripts (steps 9, 20) successfully wrote output.
trigger_explanation: The agent began step 1 with the unverified assumption that 'domain == science' was the correct filter, carried this assumption through all early scripts, and never challenged it until step 25 (when domain counter exploration was attempted). Even after correcting to biology/chemistry/physics domains (step 28), it held the false premise that only deepseek_reasoning needed to be tokenized rather than both deepseek_reasoning and deepseek_solution.
forewarning_evidence: Step 2: git clone fails with 'command not found'; steps 3-5: all attempts to read README from cloned directory fail; steps 8-10: multiple python scripts run with '(command not found in terminal output)' suggesting the scripts are not producing visible output, indicating issues with the execution approach.
